Four MD approaches agree on a conductivity of 0.171-0.181 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, about 16% above the harmonic Allen-Feldman value for the same model, and the Wigner formulation bridges the two: with classical statistics, it agrees with MD to within 5%. We trace this anharmonic enhancement to vibrational couplings that grow with the frequency difference between modes, so that anharmonic broadening opens additional channels for heat conduction. A comparison with silica, alumina, and disordered carbons reveals three regimes, in which anharmonicity reduces, barely affects, or enhances the conductivity. The predicted glass-like increase of the conductivity with temperature is consistent with thermoreflectance measurements. These results show that anharmonicity has no universal effect in disordered solids, and can promote rather than limit heat transport in strongly disordered materials.

title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
abstract: Native vacancy populations in transition-metal nitride coatings reflect vacancy formation, association, and depth-dependent stability. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compare these effects in rocksalt TiN and CrN in bulk and at (001) surfaces, within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges. In TiN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ is favoured under N-poor and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ under N-rich conditions; in CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ remains preferred throughout its stability range. Association energies are referenced to corresponding isolated vacancies where positive values mean association lowers the energy and negative values favour separation. Mean bulk association energies for mixed metal-nitrogen pairs are $+0.132$ eV in TiN and $+1.053$ eV in CrN. At (001) surfaces, $V_\mathrm{N}$ in TiN prefers the surface and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ the first subsurface layer. In CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ has similar formation energies at the surface and first subsurface layer, with a slight preference for the latter; $V_\mathrm{Cr}$ slightly prefers the second subsurface layer. Surface cluster energies are referenced to separated vacancies at their preferred depths. The compact $2V_\mathrm{Ti}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ cluster in TiN has favourable association in bulk ($+0.217$ eV per vacancy) but unfavourable association at the surface ($-0.346$ eV per vacancy). By contrast, $2V_\mathrm{Cr}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ in CrN remains stabilised, with its association energy decreasing from $+1.188$ to $+0.431$ eV per vacancy. CrN's stronger association occurs without larger structural distortions and is accompanied by distinct Cr-centred magnetic responses.

title: Nanoparticles with a BANG: Detonation-Driven Synthesis of Metals and Metal Oxides
abstract: Bristol Accelerated Nanoparticle Generation (BANG) method is a solvent- and capping-agent-free nanoparticle synthesis. Previous work was limited mostly to gold, silver and copper particles. Here, the method is extended to ten further elements, including Pb, Bi, Tl, Mn, Fe, Zn, Pt, Ni, Cd and Pd. Detonation in air favoured metal formation for less oxophilic metals, whereas detonation of silver azide under nitrogen suppressed detectable silver oxide formation while retaining locally identified hexagonal close-packed (HCP) Ag alongside face-centred cubic (FCC) Ag. The outcome of the synthesis can be modified by changing the detonation environment, while the highly non-equilibrium conditions provide access to phases that are difficult to obtain using conventional synthetic routes. BANG is a broadly applicable, highly non-equilibrium nanoparticle synthesis method whose products are governed by precursor chemistry and atmosphere, with potential access to kinetically trapped phases and direct supported-particle deposition.

title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the π-conjugated spacers
abstract: The nature of the π-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.

title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
abstract: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance. For two zero-mean Gaussian modes with circular marginals, all unperturbed intensity moments of second or third order are blind to coexistence. In contrast, a balanced fourth-order residual provides a necessary and sufficient witness. Their identities, however, remain fundamentally ambiguous: recovering the two correlation strengths does not reveal which belongs to the covariance and which to the pseudocovariance. Unexpectedly, adding thermal fluctuations resolves this ambiguity: an independent, correlated thermal probe selectively modifies the covariance while leaving the pseudocovariance unchanged, allowing the two correlation strengths to be individually identified. Moreover, a coherent reference in only one arm then makes their relative phase accessible through third-order intensity correlation. Together, these measurements reconstruct a correlation ellipse and its Poincaré-sphere coordinates, determining the relative channel strengths and the ellipse orientation. The framework separates what intensity detection can witness, what thermal probing can identify, and what a single phase reference can orient, turning inaccessible Gaussian correlation structure into a quantitatively reconstructible geometry.

title: Emission regimes and characteristic energy scales in reverse-biased 4H-SiC Schottky barriers: unified field-emission formulas and energy-dependent tunneling effective mass
abstract: Reverse leakage in 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes is analyzed using a current integral with Fermi-Dirac supply and WKB transmission. The ratio of the interface field to a critical field $F_c$ sets the depth of the thermionic-field-emission (TFE) saddle point. The Airy energy distinguishes the thermionic-tunneling crossover, the validity of the TFE formula, and the TFE/field-emission (FE) boundary, which generalizes to $c_1 k_B T \approx 1$ for arbitrary barrier shapes. Closed-form FE and TFE expressions are given for triangular and quadratic barriers; for the latter, the Padovani-Stratton formulas give 1.4-7.9 times (FE, $10^{19}$ cm$^{-3}$) and 2.5-3.6 times (TFE, low-doped layers, 300-433 K) the WKB current, whereas the present expressions agree within 15% and 2%. Applied to Ti/4H-SiC data (30-160 °C, 50-950 V), an energy-dependent tunneling mass from the complex band structure reduces the residual from 0.17 to 0.11-0.12 dex; it can be implemented in device simulation via the Franz two-band dispersion.

title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
abstract: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm^2 and 66 kA/cm^2 for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um^2 and 3 x 10 um^2, respectively. The specific contact resistance for base is estimated 1.32 x 10^{-2} Ohm.cm^2. The open-base breakdown voltage is characterized ~63 V for a 300 nm collector without dielectric passivation. This work lays the foundation for future development of N-polar III-Nitride HBTs for next-generation RF applications.

title: Compact Slow-Wave Hybrid Magnonics on Ultrahigh-Permittivity Substrates
abstract: Hybrid magnonics based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) enables strong, broadband magnon-photon coupling, but the centimeter-scale device footprints required at low gigahertz frequencies hinder integration. Here, we demonstrate miniaturized slow-wave hybrid magnonic devices using an ultrahigh-permittivity ceramic substrate ($\varepsilon = 140$). Owing to the inverse-square-root dependence of the SSPP plasma frequency on effective permittivity, the required corrugation finger length is reduced by nearly a factor of four compared with conventional microwave substrates. The ceramic is thick and brittle, and conventional thin-film processes cannot easily pattern thick, low-loss conductors on it. We overcome this challenge with additively manufactured electronics (AME). In a customized AME workflow, a multi-material inkjet printer first prints a dielectric fixture that holds and registers the ceramic. After the ceramic is loaded, the printer prints thick silver SSPP patterns directly onto it. Measurements on six printed devices with different finger lengths confirm the predicted geometry-frequency scaling. Moreover, the enhanced field confinement of the compact SSPP waveguide nearly doubles the magnon-photon coupling strength and yields ultrastrong coupling with $g/f_\mathrm{p} \approx 22\%$. Notably, this performance is achieved using a YIG film whose magnetic volume is more than an order of magnitude smaller than that employed in previous SSPP demonstrations. These results establish AME on ultrahigh-permittivity substrates as a practical route toward compact, strongly coupled hybrid magnonic devices.

title: Ultra-Wideband Stacked Patch Antenna for D-Band Applications
abstract: This article proposes a wideband stacked dual-patch antenna designed for D-band applications. The antenna is demonstrated with both wireless and dielectric waveguide (DWG) channels. The patch dimensions and spacings are chosen to ensure that the $10~dB$ return loss (RL) bandwidth covers the entire D-band ($110$--$170~GHz$). The antenna is fabricated on a seven-layer organic packaging technology. The patches are fabricated on layers 1 and 3 within a shielding cavity formed by closely spaced vias of $< λ/20$ pitch. The fabrication technology supports direct chip-level excitation of the antenna using a flip-chip packaging interface, and the design methodology for this feeding approach is outlined in the paper. In the fabricated design, however, a transition to the WR6 metallic waveguide with ($<~1~dB$) insertion loss (IL) is incorporated for feeding. This facilitates alignment and measurement of the structure using external test equipment. The full antenna and transition are integrated in a back-to-back configuration, achieving a measured $10~dB$ return loss bandwidth of more than $60~GHz$ ($110$--$170~GHz$) for the wireless link, thereby covering the entire D-band. To the best of our knowledge, this is the widest antenna bandwidth reported in the same frequency range. The measured peak gain is $8.5~dBi$ (35$^\circ$ H-plane $3~dB$ beamwidth) with a gain variation of $3.5~dBi$ within the operating bandwidth. For the dielectric waveguide configuration, the measured $10~dB$ RL bandwidth also exceeds $60~GHz$, fully encompassing the D-band. The simulated insertion loss coupling into the dielectric waveguide is $3.5~dB$. A 1-meter dielectric waveguide channel fed with the proposed antenna is measured. The overall channel exhibits a total insertion loss of $14.7~dB$, of which a simulated $3.5~dB$ at $140~GHz$ is attributed to the loss of each side that feeds the DWG.

title: Solute-Aware Stochastic Korhonen Model of Electromigration in Wide vs Near-Bamboo Al-Cu Lines
abstract: We couple an evolving Cu field to the one-dimensional Korhonen stress equation on random grain maps for wide (10 $μ$m), narrow (3 $μ$m) and near-bamboo Al-Cu lines. Earlier random-microstructure simulations fixed the Cu effect, and most continuum solute models used prescribed structures with all Cu mobile; we join the two and let only dissolved Cu move, the excess staying as immobile precipitate. With $10^3$ maps per condition at 200 $^\circ$C, we report nucleation times and sites, immortal fractions and Black's-law parameters. In cathode-limited lines Cu depletion shortens the median nucleation time 1.15- to 1.20-fold relative to immobile Cu for the cited Cu diffusivity; treating all Cu as mobile overstates this a further 2.24- to 2.36-fold at 2 wt%; the exponent stays near 2. In wide lines with reservoir ends, Cu steps left by the immobile precipitate become the failure sites, removing their Cu-free immortality if a quarter or more of the precipitate blocks Al diffusion. With Cu above the solvus the lifetime is not Arrhenius, as the dissolved fraction rises with temperature: a Black's-law fit at 250 to 300 $^\circ$C overestimates the median nucleation time at 150 $^\circ$C up to 2.33-fold at 2 wt% Cu with an exponent near 2. At the test durations the model qualitatively matches the cathode-side damage in narrow lines and the Cu build-up and mid-line peaks in wide lines but not the cathode-side Cu peaks or longer lives of narrow lines.

title: A Highly Tunable (Ti,Zr)N$_x$-Based MIM Plasmonic Sensor for Multidomain Biological, Chemical, and Physical Sensing
abstract: Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) plasmonic refractive index (RI) sensors have attracted considerable attention for label-free, real-time analyte detection; however, their reliance on noble metals such as gold and silver imposes fundamental constraints on tunability, thermal stability, and CMOS process compatibility. In this work, we propose a novel MIM plasmonic RI sensor based on a square ring resonator with embedded circular nanorods, employing the ternary nitride (Ti,Zr)N$_x$ as the plasmonic material, marking its first application in a MIM sensing platform. Compared to binary nitrides and other alternative plasmonic materials reported in the literature, (Ti,Zr)N$_x$ offers broader compositional tunability and greater flexibility in tailoring the optical response while remaining fully CMOS-compatible. The sensor is validated across a comprehensive range of biosensing and physicochemical analyte scenarios, including glucose monitoring for diabetes assessment, hemoglobin-based anemia classification across four severity levels, simultaneous discrimination of five major blood constituents, and cancer cell identification across six tissue types. For physical and chemical sensing, the structure achieves an air pressure sensitivity of 6.158 nm/MPa with negligible thermal cross-sensitivity, and a CO$_2$ detection sensitivity of 330.12 pm/ppm via polyhexamethylene biguanide (PHMB) functionalization, which is the highest reported among comparable structures in the literature. The proposed sensor achieves a maximum RI sensitivity of 2146.496 nm/RIU with a detection limit of $4.669 \times 10^{-7}$ RIU, outperforming previously reported CMOS-compatible plasmonic RI sensors.

title: Signatures of Kitaev quantum spin liquid states in $α$-RuCl$_3$ revealed by nitrogen-vacancy spin-noise spectroscopy
abstract: Bond-dependent magnetic interactions, strong spin-orbit coupling, and quantum fluctuations in $α$-RuCl$_3$ make it an archetypical candidate for exotic Kitaev quantum spin liquid (QSL) states. While electronic transport, neutron scattering, optical and tunneling spectroscopies were used to probe global QSL signatures in large scale $α$-RuCl$_3$ samples, nanoscale evidence of local QSL behavior via a non-invasive experimental probe is still missing. Here, we use diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin-noise spectroscopy to probe QSL states in α-RuCl3 nanoflakes with thicknesses ranging from 8 to 150 nm over a temperature range of 4.3-250 K. Our measurements reveal a pronounced decrease in the NV spin-lattice relaxation time ($T_{1}$) below ~100 K in proximity to the $α$-RuCl$_3$ flakes, indicating enhanced GHz-frequency magnetic fluctuations. This temperature scale is consistent with the energy scale associated with Kitaev interactions (~8 meV) and the emergence of low-energy fractionalized excitations. Below 50 K, thicker (> 90 nm) flakes exhibit a distinct bi-exponential $T_{1}$ decay, unlike the single-exponential behavior observed for off-flake and thinner (8 nm) flake measurements, suggesting an increasingly heterogeneous magnetic noise environment. These results establish NV spin-noise spectroscopy as a local, non-invasive probe of low-energy spin dynamics in $α$-RuCl$_3$ nanoflakes and open a route to testing predicted noise signatures of fractionalized excitations in atomically thin QSL candidates.

title: Multistable Thermoelectric Josephson Automata
abstract: Multistable systems can store and process information, yet their elements usually only burn the drive energy. Here, we build an automaton whose elements actively convert heat into electrical power. Heat alone stabilizes the states at zero bias, and each state routes generation and dissipation to different junctions. The elements, gap-asymmetric superconducting tunnel junctions, deliver up to 2.6 pW at either polarity under fixed heating and support a magnetic-field-tunable Josephson current. Two junctions sharing a heated island split the bias hysteretically and, even at zero bias, lock into opposite voltages encoding the sweep direction. With a load and current bias, the automaton accesses states spanning junction polarity combinations, including zero voltage; the magnetic field sets which are available and the bias history selects the occupied one.

title: Recovery of Extended Modes from the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Due to Local Nonlinearity on a Boundary
abstract: Localization in continuum spectra known as the non-Hermitian skin effect is widely believed to be a consequence of nontrivial topology of bulk bands. However, the robustness of the non-Hermitian skin effect against nonlinear effects is still a nontrivial problem. We here reveal that single-bond nonlinearity on a boundary can recover extended modes in a non-Hermitian tight-binding model. We propose and analyze a one-dimensional minimal model, where we introduce a nonlinear phase shift of a hopping term only at boundary sites. We also propose a possible photonic setup to dynamically observe the nonlinearity-induced extended modes as a steady state. Our results thus challenge the conventional notion of the non-Hermitian skin effect by revealing its dependence on nonlinear boundary conditions.

title: Intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect in ferroaxial metals with high-order rotation axes
abstract: The low-field Hall resistivity of non-magnetic metals has an intrinsic quantum contribution that derives from the field-corrected Berry curvature and intrinsic magnetic moment of the Bloch states near the Fermi surface. However, its effect is usually overshadowed by the classical Lorentz-force contribution. Here we show that for the longitudinal Hall effect, which occurs in ferroaxial crystals when the applied magnetic field lies in the Hall plane, the Lorentz force contribution vanishes for the eight ferroaxial groups with a 3,4 or 6-fold rotation axis. This provides an opportunity to measure the quantum correction in isolation, but so far all measured instances of the effect fall in the remaining five ferroaxial groups of lower symmetry, where the Lorentz force dominates the signal. We compile a list of candidate ferroaxial metals with such high-order rotation axis and compute the Hall effect from first principles for representative candidates, identifying Ni$_3$P with $σ^{\rm H}_{xzx} = 28.4$ S/m/T as a promising material to unambiguously measure the intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect.

title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
abstract: We study the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|Ω_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $Δ_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|Ω_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.

title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
abstract: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. These results suggest that PyRUA-Dex is an effective framework for developing dexterous manipulation policies with coding agents in the absence of high quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.

title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Level 4 autonomous vehicles require fault-tolerant architectures that preserve critical driving functions under sensing, computing, communication, power, and actuation failures. As these systems progress toward industrial scalability, architectural complexity, validation burden, integration effort, and lifecycle cost become increasingly relevant. This study proposes an Operational Design Domain (ODD)-based, safety-constrained systems-engineering framework for architecture rationalization. ODD-specific capabilities, physical fault assumptions, post-fault operational policies, and spatial sensing requirements are propagated through an integrated safety-feasibility gate. Architecture transformations, including removal, relocation, functional reassignment, and consolidation, are evaluated only within the resulting safety-feasible design space, followed by lifecycle-cost sensitivity and robust multiobjective Pareto analysis. A generic, synthetically parameterized Level 4 architecture is used as a demonstrative computational case study. Within this modeled design space, direct ablation showed limited rationalization potential, whereas directional redistribution and functional consolidation generated a broader set of safety-feasible candidates. Under the illustrative lifecycle-cost model, the best nominal candidate achieved a 5.55% normalized cost reduction and remained cost-reducing across all 5,000 sampled points in the prescribed uncertainty domain. The analysis identified 15 non-dominated architecture-policy solutions representing seven physical transformations. The results support capability-based, policy-conditioned, and lifecycle-aware architecture rationalization under the stated assumptions, with safety retained as a non-compensatory feasibility constraint. The reported transformations are design candidates rather than validated production architectures.

title: An exponential-rate consensus-based algorithms for estimation from relative measurements: implementation and performance analysis
abstract: In this work we address the problem of optimal estimating the position of each agent in a network from relative noisy vectorial distances with its neighbors. Although the problem can be cast as a standard least-squares problem, the main challenge is to devise scalable algorithms that allow each agent to estimate its own position by means of only local communication and bounded complexity, independently of the network size and topology. We first propose a synchronous consensus-based algorithm that is guaranteed to have exponentially convergence rate to the optimal centralized least-squares solution. We then extend this algorithm to more realistic asynchronous implementations via the use of local memory variables. We show that exponential convergence is still guaranteed under both uniform persistent communication and randomized persistent communication protocols. We finally complement the analytical results with some numerical simulations.

title: Compositional Reachset-Conformant Modeling for Managing Uncertainty in the Development of Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The development of cyber-physical systems (CPS) proceeds through iterative design revisions, and compliance with safety requirements must be re-established after every revision, typically based on a system model. Conventional models, however, predict only the most likely behavior, leading to model-plant mismatch that often surfaces only during late-stage testing, when redesign is most expensive. This article presents reachset-conformant modeling as a framework for managing uncertainty throughout the development process: instead of a single trajectory, a reachset-conformant model predicts a set of behaviors, calibrated from data to conservatively enclose the true system behavior with a statistical guarantee. Safety properties established on the model therefore transfer to the realized system. Beyond a practical introduction to reachset-conformant identification and its benefits for CPS development, our main theoretical contribution is a closure result: reachset conformance is preserved under serial composition, parallel composition, and feedback interconnection, and hence under any architecture assembled from these primitives. Subsystem models identified independently from local measurements can thus be substituted into the system architecture, and the interconnected model inherits a coverage guarantee from the subsystem guarantees. We complement this result with update strategies that adapt the uncertainty sets after design changes without restarting the identification workflow. Experiments on an automotive brake-system test bench demonstrate that a) a single model covers all operating conditions and hardware variants, b) late-stage modifications are absorbed by uncertainty set updates, c) a black-box hydraulic unit is conservatively abstracted from input-output data alone, and d) independently identified subsystem models form a conformant model by construction.

title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generalize once the DC configuration changes. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive EMT-level digital twin for DCs based on in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs). We formulate the EMT prediction task as a system identification problem under parametric uncertainty and develop a GPT-2-based framework that adapts to unseen DC configurations at inference time from a small set of EMT trajectory samples, without model retraining. The proposed framework is validated on three representative EMT scenarios and benchmarked against three baseline non-adaptive twins. Results demonstrate superior prediction accuracy, improved adaptability to unseen operating conditions, and substantial computational speedups compared to high-fidelity EMT simulation.

title: Space Postman and ATLAS: Enabling Startup Participation in the Orbital Logistics Economy
abstract: Debris removal, in-orbit servicing and refuelling, last-mile delivery, in-space recycling and constellation deployment are separate businesses built on one planning problem: a single spacecraft must visit many targets whose orbital planes drift apart under Earth's oblateness, within a propellant tank and a deadline. Solving it well takes orbital dynamics and optimisation expertise that is rarely the core business of payload, tug or constellation companies; this keeps young operators out of orbital logistics or leaves them with costly hand-made schedules. This paper presents Space Postman, a planning service that turns a target list, a spacecraft and a time budget into a priced and, for rendezvous tours, verified mission plan, and ATLAS, a tug concept whose payload bay takes debris kits, client spacecraft or propellant. As most start-ups fail when the money runs out, the offer starts with software and adds the vehicle later. Two case studies show what it changes. For a notional follow-on to the DEXTER project, which develops ways to turn scrap aluminium into propellant, it plans a tour of ten high-risk upper stages that share one orbital shell: waiting alone cannot close the tour, an even split of the time costs a third more propellant, and time is the currency of the mission. For a tug that releases eight clients from one rideshare, the delivery order decides whether the tank suffices, and the plan prices each delivery by the plane it must reach. The planning engine reproduces the published winning solution of a public debris-removal benchmark at that solution's fidelity and, given the same launches, plans cheaper trajectories for most of them: an independent check for operators and investors. A calibrated planner paired with a payload-agnostic tug offers new operators a practical way into orbital logistics, provided its numbers are read at the fidelity at which they were obtained.

title: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport
abstract: Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. To address this issue, we investigate a mirror flow approach that effectively preconditions the dual energy functional. We establish the geometric convergence of the mirror descent sequence. To obtain a practical numerical algorithm, we introduce a feasible discrete-time scheme based on first-order linearization. We prove that the scheme is well-defined and establish a uniform-in-time error bound for the accumulated linearization error, under a suitable smallness condition on the initial error. Finally, we apply the proposed mirror flow scheme to the specific-entropic martingale optimal transport (SEMOT) problem \cite{BuetGolfouseEtAl2026SEMOT} and observe a substantial improvement in computational efficiency.

title: NABLA: A Noise-Adaptive Blockwise Left-Right Preconditioning Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization
abstract: We propose NABLA, a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for mini-batch stochastic nonconvex optimization. NABLA combines an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients with block-diagonal row and column preconditioners constructed from matrix-valued second-moment statistics. Unlike conventional matrix-preconditioned methods that use fixed decay parameters, NABLA adjusts the second-moment averaging coefficient through a closed-loop feedback rule determined by the cumulative stochastic-gradient energy and its running average. The first-moment coefficient remains fixed, allowing the trajectory-dependent adaptation to act directly on the structured preconditioners. The resulting method is horizon-free, requires no prior knowledge of the noise level, and automatically adjusts the memory of its second-moment estimators to the observed optimization dynamics. Under standard lower boundedness, smoothness, unbiasedness, bounded-variance, and spectral-boundedness assumptions, we establish uniform stability and variation bounds for the time-varying block preconditioners and control their interaction with momentum estimation and parameter updates. These results yield the noise-adaptive stationarity guarantee $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2}+σ^{1/2}T^{-1/4})$, which automatically reduces to the nearly deterministic $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ rate when the stochastic-gradient noise vanishes. NABLA therefore provides a principled approach to combining closed-loop trajectory feedback with memory-efficient structured matrix preconditioning.

title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysis is a fine-grained characterization of the stochastic large-stepsize dynamics. This sharper control of the trajectory further yields tight convergence guarantees within the stable regime, improving existing bounds even in the deterministic setting. Taken together, our results show that the acceleration mechanism induced by large stepsizes survives stochasticity and extends beyond linear models. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefits of large learning rates in practice.

title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
abstract: Superfluids, in a spinning-down container with pinning centres, exhibit sudden collective migration of quantized vortices. The onset, progress, and termination of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we show that: 1) the first exodus of vortices occurs when a sector of the vortex array, having a minimum opening angle, is vacated close to the wall; 2) driven by this exodus, the superfluid flow near the boundary continually decreases in strength and arrests the exit; and 3) the resultant depletion region has well-defined dimensions---governed primarily by the critical unpinning velocity, the container size, and the initial rotation rate---that limit the angular momentum transferred to the container. We conclude by discussing the relevance to pulsar glitches.

title: Nonlinear non-modal stability and minimal perturbations in electroconvection driven by unipolar injection
abstract: Electroconvection in a dielectric liquid subjected to unipolar charge injection is subcritical. Convection can be sustained well below the threshold of linear stability theory, and experiments report onset far below it. We use nonlinear non-modal optimization to determine the smallest charge perturbations that trigger convection below the linear threshold. The method, based on a direct--adjoint formulation of the full electrohydrodynamic equations, recovers the classical linear threshold in the limit of small amplitudes. At finite amplitude, the most dangerous perturbations are localized charge deficits rather than excesses, because a deficit relaxes more slowly under Coulomb repulsion. The minimal perturbation needed for transition grows from about 0.5% of the injected charge near the linear threshold to 3% at two thirds of it, where the convective branch ends, in agreement with direct numerical simulations. Near the critical amplitude, trajectories approach an unstable steady state, the edge state, that separates the basins of attraction of rest and convection and originates from the critical linear mode. The damped oscillatory modes involved in the growth of the optimal perturbations are transit-time modes of the ion drift. The convective mode is the first of them, made stationary by the coupling with the flow, which explains why the instability sets in as a steady motion. Small charge fluctuations can therefore lower the onset of electroconvection to about two thirds of the linear threshold, helping to explain the discrepancy between linear theory and experiments.

title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
abstract: Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by $6r_S$, independently of the discretization order, where $r_S$ is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to $2^{26}$ points. For Rayleigh-Bénard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.

title: Impact of Taylor-Aris dispersion on chemical patterns in confined channel flows
abstract: Chemical patterns form through non-linear interactions between different species. We study how confined channel flows affect pattern formation using the Brusselator as a paradigmatic activator-inhibitor model. An invariant-manifold method for slender channels reduces the advection-diffusion-reaction equation to one spatial dimension, with species transported at the mean flow velocity and molecular diffusivities replaced by the classical Taylor-Aris dispersion coefficients. We obtain the phase diagram as a function of the Péclet number (i.e., the relative strength of advection to diffusion), the channel slenderness, and the diffusivity ratio of the species. Our analytical results demonstrate that the classical Turing criterion can become inverted at large Péclet numbers and, thus, channel flow can trigger pattern formation even when the molecular diffusivities violate the classical Turing condition, and conversely destroy pre-existing patterns. Both predictions are confirmed by direct numerical simulations, which show advected stripe patterns, whose wavelength can be predicted by our reduced theory, as well as oscillatory dynamics. These findings highlight that hydrodynamic flows can modify chemical mixing and thereby profoundly affect pattern formation in channel geometries.

title: Effect of humidity and phase transition on turbulent diffusion of droplets and water vapour in atmospheric turbulent flows
abstract: We investigate the effect of humidity on turbulent diffusion of droplets and water vapour in atmospheric turbulent flows taking into account the effect of phase transitions on turbulent transport. We find that the coefficients of turbulent diffusion of droplets and water vapour decrease with increase the turbulent Damköhler number (the ratio of turbulent time in the integral scale and phase transition time for condensation of water vapour), while the coefficients of the mutual turbulent diffusion that describe the turbulent cross effects increase with this parameter. For large turbulent Damköhler number, the coefficient of turbulent diffusion of droplets is strongly depleted when the evaporation of droplets is much faster than the condensation of water vapour. The obtained theoretical relationships are potentially useful in modelling applications in the atmospheric turbulence.

title: DED-Agent: An agentic AI method for autonomous thermal simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition
abstract: In metal additive manufacturing (AM), process parameters set the local thermal history, which governs defects, microstructure and properties. Laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness, scan strategy and position combine into a design space of 10^4-10^6 conditions, which is beyond what human experts can map by hand with finite element (FE) thermal models: every model must be set up, meshed, solved and calibrated by an expert, and calibrating unknown heat-source parameters alone can take days to weeks. This paper presents DED-Agent, an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) method for autonomous simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition (L-DED). A supervisor agent coordinates three specialist agents that share a structured simulation specification and call open-source tools. An intent agent turns a plain-language request into a validated specification, a simulation agent builds, runs and checks an FE thermal model through physics-aware step-by-step reasoning, and a calibration agent identifies key heat-source parameters against experimental data (e.g., thermocouple data) using a high-order proper generalized decomposition (HOPGD) surrogate within a trust-region search. On five benchmark builds, from single-track walls to a multi-track band on a cylindrical tube, the agents built executable thermal models without manual intervention, with 4.1-9.1% error for the simple and medium builds. Within three calibration rounds, the error fell to 0.9-2.5%. The surrogate matched full FE to within 0.08-1.55% and shortened calibration by 5-13 times. Agentic AI can thus autonomously establish reliable, accurate simulation models for AM processes and accelerate the search for process parameters that control microstructure.

title: Large-Scale Streaming Portfolio Optimization with Pauli Correlation Encoding
abstract: Classical portfolio construction over large asset universes is a combinatorial selection problem that existing heuristics do not solve well at scale. Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) addresses this by representing the underlying clustering problem with far fewer qubits than one per asset, and a prior study showed it is competitive with classical methods on a single historical snapshot. This paper moves beyond that static test to a streaming deployment, in which the correlation structure and the portfolio are both re-estimated on a rolling basis, as a live rebalancing system would actually operate. We introduce two streaming variants -- PCE itself and a joint multi-cut variant, dPCE -- and evaluate both against a Buy & Hold baseline across window lengths, portfolio sizes up to several thousand assets, risk-aversion and transaction-cost settings, and measurement-shot budgets. Streaming PCE and dPCE consistently outperform the passive baseline, including during a market downturn where both lose money but PCE loses markedly less -- evidence that the method's value is not confined to rising markets. PCE also proves the more practical choice at scale, since dPCE's resource requirements and its sensitivity to rebalancing frequency both grow faster with portfolio size. We further report which operational choices -- rebalancing cadence, shot budget, and transaction-cost awareness -- matter most for a real deployment, and which matter less than commonly assumed.

title: Accuracy and Efficiency of Lowest-order and Higher-Order Single-Source Integral Equations
abstract: The single-source integral equation allows the modeling of the electromagnetic field by only tracking a single surface-supported current density. It features products of integral operators, which pose unique challenges for the modeler in both the discretization and solution of the equation. Due to the unique structure of the single-source equation, its conforming and stable discretization requires expanding one of the two physical traces in primal basis functions and the other in dual basis functions. Primal functions are expected to have better approximation properties than dual ones. In this work, we study the impact of this asymmetric representation on the accuracy of the solution and propose an approach from which both traces can be recovered using only primal functions with modest additional computational cost. Moreover, we propose an alternative discretization scheme based on approximating the inverse of the duality mapping induced by the surface normal cross-product operator through the quasi-Helmholtz decomposition. This discretization provides greater flexibility in the choice of function spaces, enabling both a higher-order extension of the single-source equation and a more efficient lowest-order discretization using only Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. Numerical results show the impact of the representation in terms of primal and dual functions in both lowest- and higher-order discretization.

title: Low-Frequency Stable Single-Source Integral Equation
abstract: Among the integral equations for scattering by homogeneous dielectric objects, single-source integral equations (SSIEs) provide the advantage of having only a single electric or magnetic current unknown. A well-conditioned SSIE can be obtained by appropriately combining the interior and exterior Calderón formulas. The condition number of the resulting operator appearing in the well-conditioned SSIE remains bounded at low frequencies. However, SSIEs still suffer from low-frequency cancellation, causing loss of significant digits in the solution, the right-hand side, and the system matrix. In this work, we apply a rescaling strategy based on quasi-Helmholtz projectors to the well-conditioned SSIE. Primal and dual space projectors are required since both primal and dual spaces are used to discretize the SSIE operators. We show that the solution of the rescaled SSIE is immune to catastrophic cancellations at low frequencies. Numerical experiments corroborate the method by testing the accuracy of the radiated field for extremely low frequencies.
